presetPolicy.storageModel: One versioned localStorage root per supported tool. Records use generated identifiers and validated tool-owned configurations.

candidates.currentStateModel: Configured total milliseconds plus remaining milliseconds and a running flag; minutes and seconds are editable while stopped.
candidates.shareValue: High: a recipient can reproduce an exact countdown duration.
candidates.presetValue: High: repeated custom durations are common and the configuration is one bounded scalar.

candidates.currentStateModel: Work, short-break, long-break, cycle, cue, phase, remaining, and running state.
candidates.shareValue: High: timing and cue choices form a meaningful reusable routine.
candidates.presetValue: High: users may switch between several focus and break patterns.

candidates.currentStateModel: One to many user-labeled steps, per-step durations, rounds, active index, current round, remaining time, and running/completed state.
candidates.shareValue: Moderate, but the labels are necessary to understand the sequence and can contain arbitrary private text.
candidates.presetValue: High in principle, but a safe preset would need a label policy and array migration work beyond the selected scalar infrastructure.
candidates.exclusionReason: Excluded because the meaningful configuration depends on arbitrary user labels and an array schema; omitting labels loses meaning while including them conflicts with the privacy-first URL scope.

candidates.currentStateModel: Warm-up, work, rest, rounds, cool-down, cue settings, current step, round index, remaining time, and running state.
candidates.shareValue: High: the fixed phase model can be represented safely without labels.
candidates.presetValue: High: workout timing patterns are commonly reused.

candidates.currentStateModel: Persistent user-titled agenda items, durations, active item, remaining time, and running state.
candidates.existingPersistence: Agenda items are already restored automatically from localStorage.
candidates.shareValue: Low under the privacy rules because meaningful links would contain agenda text.
candidates.presetValue: Limited incremental value because the current agenda already persists; named copies would encourage storage of meeting notes.
candidates.exclusionReason: Excluded because agenda titles may contain private meeting information and the route already persists the active agenda locally.

candidates.currentStateModel: Source zone, destination zone, date, time, seconds visibility, rendered resolution, and locally persisted preferences.
candidates.existingPersistence: Preferences restore from localStorage; the existing share link currently overrides them on load.
candidates.shareValue: Already implemented and valuable; Stage 6 must version and strictly validate it while preventing automatic persistence of shared input.
candidates.presetValue: Low: the route already restores its most recent conversion and the meeting planner owns reusable timezone groups.
candidates.exclusionReason: Named presets are excluded because existing preference restoration covers the repeated-use case without adding another storage model.

candidates.currentStateModel: UTC reference date, duration, work window, one to eight IANA zones, and derived candidates.
candidates.shareValue: High: a recipient can reproduce the same zone comparison without private labels.
candidates.presetValue: High: named timezone groups and work windows are useful for recurring teams.

candidates.currentStateModel: One to twelve named events with target local date-times, selected event, sound choices, remaining time, and status.
candidates.existingPersistence: The complete event collection already restores from localStorage.
candidates.shareValue: Moderate, but useful links would expose arbitrary event names and collection state.
candidates.presetValue: Low incremental value because events are already named and persist locally.
candidates.exclusionReason: Excluded because event names can be private and the route already provides named persistent events rather than reusable configuration presets.

candidates.currentStateModel: One to eight labeled timers with configured and remaining milliseconds, run/alarm state, sound settings, and target timestamps.
candidates.existingPersistence: The timer collection and active timing state already restore from localStorage.
candidates.shareValue: Moderate, but a safe ready-state representation would either expose labels or strip essential context.
candidates.presetValue: Moderate, but the current collection already persists and separating configuration from live state requires a dedicated collection migration.
candidates.exclusionReason: Excluded because labels may be private, the existing storage includes transient live state, and a safe named-template model should not be layered onto that payload in this stage.

candidates.currentStateModel: A route-local zone list and live derived clock rows.
candidates.shareValue: Moderate, but the meeting planner provides a more meaningful shareable multi-zone task.
candidates.presetValue: Moderate, but timezone groups are implemented once on the meeting planner to avoid duplicate preset systems.
candidates.exclusionReason: Excluded to keep timezone-group sharing and presets on the meeting planner, where date, duration, and work-window context make the setup actionable.

analyticsAndTransmissionReview.analyticsImplementation: app/clients/lib/analytics.ts sends path-only pageviews and allowlisted custom event properties after consent. Full URLs, query strings, preset names, and configuration fields are not intentionally included.
analyticsAndTransmissionReview.sharedUrlDisclosure: A recipient and services involved in transporting or requesting a shared URL can read its selected settings. Share links therefore exclude notes, names, history, and transient state.
analyticsAndTransmissionReview.presetTransmission: Preset CRUD uses browser localStorage only and adds no external request or custom analytics payload.
